page: Microsoft Azure M16bs_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the MBSMediumMemoryv3 family. Powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8473C processor running at 4.0 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes a 105 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix operations. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is not bundled, meaning the instance relies entirely on external block storage, though it is premium storage capable.

Benchmark results show strong single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2213.0 placing it in the top 10% tier. Single-threaded gzip compression at 32.93 GB/sec and Geekbench text processing at 2801.0 both rank in the top 25%. Multi-core performance, such as stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, falls within the average range. Memory bandwidth is measured at 1383.1 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 108.38 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. For machine learning workloads, the instance achieves a strong text generation speed of 333.36 tokens/second on a small 135M LLM model, while larger models perform in the average tier.

From a resource density perspective, the M16bs_v3 offers a qualitative balance for memory-intensive workloads that do not require local NVMe storage. The dedicated CPU allocation and large L3 cache ensure consistent performance, though the lack of integrated local storage requires external block storage provisioning. This server is suited for memory-intensive applications, database hosting, enterprise software, text processing pipelines, and moderate-scale language model inference.
